name: Pull-up
pattern: Vertical pull: hanging from a bar, the arms pull the body up until the chin passes the bar, shoulder blades pulling down and back.
setup: Hands on the bar a little wider than your shoulders, palms away (palms toward you for a chin-up).
Hang with arms straight, legs together, ribs down.
Before you bend your arms, pull your shoulders down away from your ears.

steps.text: Start from straight arms, body still.
Pull your shoulder blades down and slightly back; you rise a few centimetres with straight arms.
Drive your elbows down toward your ribs until your chin clears the bar.
Chest toward the bar, shoulders down, no chin poke.
Lower under control all the way to straight arms.

cues.cue: Shoulders down and back before the arms bend.
cues.why: The lower trapezius fires first and starts the pull; it is more active in the pull-up than the chin-up.

cues.cue: Drive your elbows down to your back pockets.
cues.why: The lats are the main mover (over 100% MVIC in testing) and finish the pull with the biceps.

cues.cue: Hands just outside your shoulders; avoid very wide or behind-the-neck pulls.
cues.why: Wide and palms-toward pulls showed shoulder positions linked with impingement risk; shoulder-width front pulls are safer.

cues.cue: Ribs down, legs together, no swing.
cues.why: The trunk muscles work to keep the body still; swinging turns it into a different, kipping skill.

cues.cue: Straight arms at the bottom, chin over the bar at the top.
cues.why: Full elbow range is about 90-100° in a strict rep; partial reps cut the work done.

breathing: Breathe out as you pull up, in as you lower.

tempo.note: Pull in about 1 second, short pause, lower in 2 to 3.

mistakes.name: Shoulders shrug up
mistakes.looks: Shoulders ride up to the ears and the neck disappears at the top.
mistakes.fix: Pull your shoulders down first and keep them down.
mistakes.why: Pulling with elevated shoulder blades reduces space under the acromion at high arm angles.

mistakes.name: Half reps
mistakes.looks: Arms never straighten at the bottom, or the chin never reaches the bar.
mistakes.fix: Lower to straight arms each rep; use a band if you cannot finish.
mistakes.why: Strict reps move the elbow through about 90-100°; short reps skip the hardest part.

mistakes.name: Kipping and swinging
mistakes.looks: Knees drive up and the hips swing to throw the body to the bar.
mistakes.fix: Legs together, glutes tight, slow down; use a band or negatives if needed.
mistakes.why: Momentum shifts load away from the back muscles and adds sudden stress on the shoulder.

mistakes.name: Chin reaches
mistakes.looks: The head pokes forward and up to get the chin over the bar.
mistakes.fix: Keep a long neck and bring your chest to the bar.
mistakes.why: Reaching with the neck fakes the last few centimetres and strains the neck.

safety: Shoulder pain: use a shoulder-width or neutral grip and avoid behind-the-neck pulls.
Elbow pain: try a neutral grip or rings so the hands can turn.
Drop off with bent knees; do not let go from a high hang onto straight legs.

variants.change: Palms toward you: more biceps and chest; less lower trapezius; elbow range a little larger (about 100°).
Palms facing: overall muscle activity similar; slightly less mid trapezius than the pronated grip.
Hands about 2x shoulder width: shorter range and shoulder positions linked with more impingement risk.
Behind the neck: forces the shoulder into end-range external rotation; best avoided.
Belt or vest load; same form.
One arm does most of the work; shoulders stay level as long as you can.
Rope grip: much harder on the forearms and grip.
Rings let the hands turn; the bar path can curve.
Legs held straight out in front at 90°: adds hip flexor and abdominal work.
Ring muscle-up needs more biceps, forearm and upper-trapezius work than the bar version; learn it on the bar first.

subtypes.name: Assisted pull-up
subtypes.change: Feet on a box or floor, knee on a pad, or a band under the feet takes part of the body weight. Same arm and shoulder-blade path.

subtypes.name: Negative and hold
subtypes.match: negative|eccentric|isometric|hold|top pull up hold|half pull|top half
subtypes.change: Jump or step to the top position, then hold or lower slowly for 3-5 seconds.

subtypes.name: Dead hang
subtypes.change: Hold the bottom position for time. Passive hang: shoulders relax up. Active hang: shoulders pulled down with straight arms.

subtypes.name: Muscle-up
subtypes.change: Explosive pull to the lower chest, wrists turn over the bar or rings, then press up like a dip to straight arms. Learn on a bar before rings.

subtypes.name: Rope climb
subtypes.change: Hand over hand up a rope (feet can clamp the rope) or along monkey bars; each pull is a one-arm pull-up path with the other arm reaching up.

metrics.label: Elbow bend
metrics.good: 0-15 at the bottom, 100-120 at the top

metrics.label: Chin height
metrics.good: chin above the bar at the top

metrics.label: Shoulders down
metrics.good: below 0 from the Set phase on

motion.basis: Elbow range (about 93-100°) and the lower-trapezius-first timing from youdas2010; scapular pattern (upward rotation near 45° with arms overhead, falling to about 10° at the top; depression and retraction during the pull) from prinold2016 and escamilla2009, values rounded by us. Trunk, hip and shoulder angles estimated from video convention.
